context: WebGL-rendered density heatmap of 5 million synthetic points across 6 Gaussian clusters, with semantic zoom that cross-fades from a Gaussian-blurred heatmap to individual color-coded scatter points at high zoom levels (LOD transition at ~4x scale).
first_impression: Immediately readable — five hot spots stand out against a dark blue field with no visual clutter competing for attention.
what_works: The perceptual color ramp (dark blue → cyan → yellow → white with gamma correction) maps density intuitively, and all 5-6 cluster peaks are distinguishable at a glance without any interaction; the HUD and legend are compact and non-intrusive, leaving the data field unobstructed.
what_doesnt: The ramp terminates in white at peak density, which risks blending into the light background at cluster edges and could obscure fine density gradients near hot-spot centers; the LOD cross-fade and points-mode cluster coloring (6 Tol hues) are the main perceptual bets of this design but cannot be assessed from the static screenshot — animation congruence and color separability at high zoom are unverified.
